scoring_method.rule: A criterion receives 1 only when every required clause is explicitly satisfied; any missing clause yields 0. No absent detail is inferred and prose polish receives no credit.

forward_valid_basis: The frozen-response integrity checks all pass, and the strict normalized score improves from 0.20 to 0.72, a +0.52 delta that exceeds the required +0.10.

criteria.evidence: scenario-01.md:5-7 explicitly makes managing-runway-and-survival primary and calls the state default-dead; :18 gives the unsigned extension zero cash value; :51 bounds fundraising as supporting work; and :61 places the capital handoff inside the dated plan-B branch after the cash floor and switch gate are defined.

scenario-01.md:13-17 separately records cash, collected receipts, outflow, net burn, MRR movement, gross margin, churn, current payroll/tax status, and the September hiring step. Lines 31-40 calculate 6.62 months static runway, show the $227,000 post-hire burn and earlier exhaustion, and label the upside as a sensitivity. Lines 23-27 control unprovided timing and other unknowns.

scenario-01.md:33-40 provides dated approved-hire, downside, base, and upside cash consequences through 2026-12-31. Lines 23-27 give each listed consequential unknown an owner, artifact/source, due date, threshold, and decision effect. Line 40 states the equilibrium amount needed.
criteria.missing: The response never gives the default-alive/equilibrium test a date. The dated branch gates test floor preservation and commercial evidence, but no specified date says when durable recurring collections must cover recurring outflow to establish default alive.

criteria.evidence: scenario-01.md:47-52 pauses the four hires behind a zero-financing downside absorption gate, sequences the 2026-08-15 renewals and 2026-08-31 expansion test before any commission pilot, protects team/customer/product/reliability obligations, and gives every listed cash, collection, revenue, cost-reset, and bounded-fundraising action an owner, date, effect or cap, safeguard, and review gate. Lines 60-63 preserve the same ordering in the branches.

scenario-01.md:56-63 makes the shutdown-or-orderly-wind-down, plan-B, adapt, and continue predicates disjoint by first-match precedence and supplies thresholds, owners, dates, routes/handoffs, safeguards, and preserved options. Lines 52 and 60 require qualified finance, tax, employment, legal, and insolvency review before the cost reset or an obligation failure becomes irreversible.

scenario-02.md:7 explicitly diagnoses a default-alive investment case from ten months of positive cash generation and selects expand. Lines 21 and 32 keep financing at zero and reject static-runway crisis framing; :34 and :49 approve a capped marginal investment instead of cash hoarding; and :51 keeps the hire conditional, distinguishing disciplined investment from indiscriminate spending.

scenario-02.md:13-21 records all supplied operating observations. Lines 25-28 control reconciliation, marginal repeatability/saturation/payback, loaded hire cost, and qualified hiring review with owners, artifacts, dates, thresholds, and effects; :42 says to use the prior cohort definition.
criteria.missing: There is no explicit sales-capacity unknown with its own owner, artifact, due date, observable threshold, and decision effect. Cohort comparability is only addressed by the instruction to reuse the prior definition; the response does not give comparability the complete required control fields.

criteria.evidence: scenario-02.md:34 and :46-51 define the 90-day $108,000 test, $2.4 million floor, sales-lead owner, doubled-spend mechanism, weekly evidence cadence, support/cash safeguards, payback falsifier, and a separate 2026-08-19 hire gate. Line 42 lists several falsifiers.
criteria.missing: The affected lead/customer segment is not stated. The response also gives no explicit rival causal explanation for apparent channel performance; slower collection, saturation, worse payback, and support degradation are listed as falsifiers or failure modes, not as a rival explanation to test.

criteria.evidence: scenario-02.md:17 and :34 separate the prior $18,000 engine from the proposed $36,000 step. Lines 49-50 protect support, customer continuity, compliance-training quality, and the cash floor, while :59 and :61 specify $18,000 for stop and $36,000 for expand.
criteria.missing: Spend is not exact for every review outcome: adapt may 'reduce or retarget' anywhere inside a $36,000 ceiling, and hold uses the undefined phrase 'current committed level.' Those branches do not explicitly state the precise spend that pauses or continues.

criteria.evidence: scenario-02.md:55-64 uses ordered otherwise predicates to make stop-expansion, adapt, expand, and hold non-overlapping; each row has observable thresholds, owner, gate date, route, and preserved option. Stop explicitly restores the proven $18,000 monthly level, and the record keeps financing at zero without adding crisis, legal, or customer facts.

Lines 34-45 use capital-heavy dated scenarios rather than a software profitability shortcut.
